Questions.question: Why does the instructor check the oil level before draining it?
Questions.answer: Because it helps check the oil condition and quantity.
options: Because it helps check the draining and quantity.
Because it helps check the oil condition and quantity.
Because it helps check the oil condition and engine.

Questions.question: Why is the used oil allowed to drain completely?
Questions.answer: To avoid problems caused by old oil remaining inside.
options: To avoid problems during servicing by old oil remaining inside.
To avoid problems caused by old oil remaining inside.
To avoid problems caused by old oil under the engine.

Questions.question: Why is the new oil filter tightened by hand?
Questions.answer: Because too much force can damage the seal.
options: Because too many tools can damage the seal.
Because too much force can damage the seal.
Because too many filters can damage the seal.

Questions.question: Why is the engine run briefly after refilling oil?
Questions.answer: To check for leaks after servicing.
options: To refill the engine oil after servicing.
To check for leaks after servicing.
To increase engine speed after servicing.

Questions.question: Why does the instructor stress the correct order of brake inspection steps?
Questions.answer: Because missing steps can cause safety problems.
options: Because missing inspections can cause problems.
Because missing steps can cause safety problems.
Because missing brakes are safe.

activity_c.text: Good morning, everyone.
Let’s get started.
Today, I want to explain two routine processes that we practise in the Automobile Technology section.
First, I will explain an engine oil service.
After that, we will move on to a basic brake inspection.
Please listen carefully and follow the order of the steps.
First, let’s look at the engine oil service.
In our workshop, vehicles usually arrive early in the morning.
Before anything else, we check the engine oil level using the dipstick.
This helps us understand the oil condition and the quantity.
If the oil looks very dark or smells burnt, it usually means the oil must be changed.
Next, we place an oil tray under the engine.
Then, we drain the used engine oil.
We wait until all the oil flows out.
We do not rush this step, because old oil left inside the engine can cause problems.
After that, we remove the old oil filter carefully.
The filter often contains dirty oil, so we handle it slowly to avoid spilling oil on the floor.
Then, we fit a new oil filter.
We tighten it by hand only.
We do not use too much force, because overtightening can damage the rubber seal.
Next, we tighten the drain plug properly and refill the engine with the correct grade of oil.
Finally, we run the engine briefly and check for leaks.
If there are no leaks, the oil service is complete.
Now, let’s move to the brake inspection process.
This inspection is usually done before a test drive.
First, we check the brake fluid level in the reservoir.
If the level is low, there may be brake pad wear or a small leak.
Next, we inspect the brake hoses and connections.
After that, we remove the wheel and check the brake pads.
We look at the thickness and check for uneven wear.
Finally, we refit the wheel and tighten the wheel nuts evenly.
We always follow these steps carefully, because brake safety is very important.
Missing a step can cause serious problems later.
